review.headline: A silent Floofer hug corrupted every info report, yet the table caught it anyway
review.summary: In round 1, Blair (Mouser) claimed Hawk right after the real Hawk, Alex. The table eggsecuted Alex, and Blair took a 31-point lead. Alex was then the Floofer in rounds 2 and 3. Both times an Owl or Hawk caught his fake Hawk claim, and Farm won. Blair held the round 1 lead to finish on 69. Alex finished last on 8 after losing all three rounds. Hugs were never reported to the players hit by them, and many players misread nest sizes. Together these made a lot of wrong claims, most of them by honest Farm players.

rounds.recap: Alex (the real Hawk) and Blair (Mouser) both claimed Hawk. Blair's claimed visit to Drew fit Drew being confused, so the table took that as backing for Blair. Alex's true visit to Ellis left no trace. Alex was eggsecuted 15 cards to 1 and the cats banked 46 points.

Alex (Floofer) claimed Hawk and said he visited Blair. Drew's Owl saw only a Floofer visit Blair, which broke the claim. Casey (Mouser) collided with Finley's Kookaburra claim but escaped by joining the vote on Alex. Alex was eggsecuted and Farm won big.

Alex (Floofer) hugged Finley, and Blair got hugged by visiting him, so both Farm info reports were blank. Both players filled in results they never got. Casey misread her Turkey role and pushed Finley, and Ellis (Mouser) knew Finley was Farm and piled on too. Drew's real Hawk claim still beat Alex's copy, and Alex went out 9 cards to 7.

highlights.text: Blair copied Alex's Hawk claim seconds after hearing it, and the table eggsecuted the real Hawk.
Drew's Owl report ('only the Floofer visited Blair') was the cleanest hard evidence of the game and ended Alex's bluff.
Alex flipped round 1 around: he claimed Hawk first, then accused the real Hawk Drew of 'the same trick Blair used on me.'
The vote was close at 9 cards to 7, with Farm Casey throwing 4 cards at Farm Finley. She still banked 27 because her team won.

confusions.what: Claimed a Falcon result (Ellis visited no one, egg for me) that his report never gave him; he had been hugged. He corrected this in beat 2.
Worked out nest changes from a baseline of 5 for everyone. Nests carry over between rounds.
As Turkey, expected to see his visitors or eggs in his own nest. Turkey eggs go to the visitors, and the Turkey learns nothing.
Said 'a Turkey would know he was visited', which is false. As a cat he may have been bluffing on purpose.
Claimed an Owl result (no visitors, laid an egg in Alex's nest) that he never received. He had been hugged by visiting the Floofer and was not told.
Counted the Turkey's egg as his Eagle egg, did not notice he had been hugged, and assumed Casey went from 5 to 7. She simply carried 5 cards over and drew 2.
Thought her own nest would change if she was visited as Turkey, so she called Finley's true visit a lie and threw 4 cards at a Farm player.
Said Alex was '+3' from a baseline of 5, but Alex had carried 6 cards over and drawn 2.

design_notes: The Floofer was the strongest card. It was in play all three rounds and hugged an info role every time (Drew, Blair, Finley, plus Blair by visiting it). Hugged players are not told, so honest Farm players invented results 3 times. Either tell hugged players their action failed, or accept that the Floofer mostly makes honest players lie.

Nest sizes misled the table more than they helped. Nests carry over, but players kept computing changes from 5. Show the change since dawn, or each player's size at round start. Turkey wording also failed twice: add 'You are not told who visited you, and your nest does not change.'

The Wink was never used, even though a Mouser held it each round (Blair, Casey, Ellis). The Mouser's role info carried all of its value: Blair copied a safe story, and Ellis knew which Farm player to push. The Wink either needs a reason to fire or should be cut.

Dusk was mostly filler. Beat 2 was silent all three rounds, and beat 1 was boilerplate. But its hints mattered: Blair's and Drew's descriptions in round 2 told the Floofer whom to hug, and Finley's Kookaburra hint set up Casey's role clash. Consider a single dusk beat.

Scoring ignores accuracy when your team wins. Casey threw 4 cards at a Farm teammate and banked 27. Combined with round 1's two-cat win (46 banked), an early round can decide the game. Blair's lead from round 1 was never caught.
